figure.title: Aerodynamic characteristics of the body alone. (b) Drag coefficient.
figure.x_axis: Drag coefficient, CD, on the wing area of 1.143 sq ft (staggered: each Mach number has its own CD = 0)
figure.y_axis: Angle of attack of the body centre line, deg (common to all Mach numbers)
figure.content_note: Measured points: hollow symbols with a centre dot, one shape per Mach number, joined by faired curves.

scan.extraction: tools/digitize/extract_scan.py --turn cw: the page's single embedded image (page /Rotate 0), turned a quarter turn clockwise so that the sideways figure reads upright

calibration.x_definition: Common staggered axis: left frame 0.000, grid every 0.002, heavy line every 0.004. Each heavy line from 0.000 to 0.048 is the CD = 0 of one Mach number, in the order labelled under the axis: 0.50, 0.70, 0.85, 0.90, 0.925, 0.95, 0.975, 1.00, 1.02, 1.035, 1.085, 1.10, 1.13; then .004 .008 .012 of M 1.13 at 0.052 to 0.060 (right frame).

scope: Body-alone drag only (brief 001, Amendment 3, point 2): every symbol at the nominal angles of attack -2, 0 and 2 deg, at all 13 Mach numbers. The symbols at higher angles are not read.
assignment_method: Each Mach number has its own symbol shape and its own CD origin; the angle of attack is read on the common vertical axis. Every Mach number has two symbols near alpha 0 (a repeated test point, as near alpha 6). Pass A first read seven of these pairs as one symbol with a doubled outline; after pass B's report each was checked on the scan and the second symbol added (see the notes).
